pr_body:
Which hides the cursor if you don't use it for a while.

Fixes #1471
pr_comments:
A couple of issues when testing:
 * setting the timeout interactively doesn't affect a cursor until it moved. For example, from no timeout to some short timeout (e.g. 10ms) the cursor won't disappear until it moved.
 * setting the timeout to something really small (< 1 frame redraw time? try 10ms) will display as if the cursor didn't move when it really did move. Some slightly longer value (e.g. 100ms) work around the problem and work as expected.

>setting the timeout interactively doesn't affect a cursor until it moved. For example, from no timeout to some short timeout (e.g. 10ms) the cursor won't disappear until it moved.

Yeah, I saw this coming and was okay with it. Fixing it will make a lot of unrelated systems talk to each other.
Set the minimum to 100ms, also prevents you from setting a negative timeout.

Is there a chance this would be rebased and merged? I'm using xbanish on i3wm and this looks like a nice replacement. Or is there an alternative approach over ipc? I was trying to find something for Wayland and I found only a script which was moving the cursor to 0×0 position.

issue_context.title: Hide mouse cursor on inactivity
issue_context.body: Just like `unclutter` does for X, it would be useful to have a setting for the amount of seconds of mouse inactivity after which to hide the mouse cursor.
comments:
You can use this tool to hide your mouse under Wayland, I've just written it and I'm happily making use of it:

- https://gitlab.com/interception/linux/plugins/hideaway
Just as a PSA for anyone stumbling here, Sway can do this natively also, f.ex `seat * hide_cursor 8000`
I love how things just go away and sensible defaults are included where I need them, thank you sway
Is there something similar for when i start typing?

> @dzintars `seat * hide_cursor when-typing enable`

Can be combined with 

     seat * hide_cursor 8000

Or do you need to set both separately?

review_comments: This will set again the cursor image each time an input event is received. This is an issue with `wlr_xcursor_manager_set_cursor_image` because it'll reupload the pixels to the GPU each time.
